problem: Find the equation of the downward-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(1,1)$ and which passes through the point $(-6,-6).$
worked_solution:
For any upward or downward-opening parabola with its vertex at $(h,k),$ the general standard equation is given by

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k).
$$

Here, the vertex has coordinates $(h,k)=(1,1).$ Substituting these into the general standard equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)^{2} & =4p(y-1).\end{aligned}
$$

We are left to find the value of $p.$ We know that the given parabola also passes through the point $(-6,-6),$ so we can substitute $x=-6$ and $y=-6$ into the standard equation and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)^{2} & =4p(y-1) \\ (-6-1)^{2} & =4p(-6-1) \\ 49 & =-28p \\ p & =-\frac{7}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)^{2} & =4p(y-1) \\ (x-1)^{2} & =4(-\frac{7}{4})(y-1) \\ (x-1)^{2} & =-7(y-1).\end{aligned}
$$
